_meta: Topic queue — the human-controlled INPUT to the content engine. Topics come from real Tricity demand, never invented by the model. The engine pulls the first status:"pending" entry per run, processes exactly one, and writes the outcome back here. This file is the audit trail / proof of editorial oversight. Each topic has a lang ('en' or 'hi'); Hindi topics are drafted natively in simple Hindi (not translated) and written under <section>/hi/. Statuses: pending | published | skipped-dup | killed-commodity | halted-factcheck. NOTE: every generated image must be human-reviewed for correct vehicle type (seated step-through e-moped, not a standing kick-scooter) and context before publishing.

title: Petrol scooter vs low-speed EV in the Tricity: the real one-year cost, in rupees
imagePrompt: A 100cc petrol scooter and a seated step-through electric scooter (Indian e-moped — seat, flat floorboard, small wheels) parked side by side on a clean, tree-lined Chandigarh sector road.
angle: Work the actual year-one running cost on Chandigarh's tiered domestic tariff (~Rs 5/unit all-in) against a 100cc petrol commuter — the local power price is the ownable hook a generic petrol-vs-EV answer can't have.

title: Buying your first electric scooter in the Tricity: a plain decision guide
imagePrompt: A first-time rider standing beside a parked seated step-through electric scooter (Indian e-moped — seat, flat floorboard, small wheels) on a calm Chandigarh sector street, daytime.
angle: A decision framework keyed to daily distance and the no-licence (<=25 km/h, <=250W) exemption — route the reader to match commute km to battery type, not to a specific model.

title: Charging a low-speed EV without a garage: options for Tricity flats
imagePrompt: A resident carrying a removable scooter battery into a flat, and a charger cable plugged into an ordinary 3-pin domestic wall socket on the wall of a Chandigarh home — everyday residential setting.
angle: Practical charging for apartment and rented-accommodation riders with no private parking — removable batteries, a regular 5A/15A socket, and the ~2 units per full charge. Distinct from the home-charging-cost page: this is the 'where do I plug in' problem, not the 'what does it cost' one.

title: Why your EV scooter's real range is less than the brochure (and how to plan for it)
imagePrompt: Close-up of the handlebar and display of a seated step-through electric scooter (Indian e-moped — seat, flat floorboard, small wheels) showing the battery gauge, on a quiet tree-lined Chandigarh sector road.
angle: Explain the gap between claimed and real-world range honestly (rider weight, terrain, battery type, age) and tie it to typical Tricity commute distances so a buyer sizes the battery for the route they actually ride.

title: Lead-acid or lithium for your low-speed scooter? Match the battery to your daily km
imagePrompt: Two electric-scooter batteries side by side on a clean workshop bench — a heavier lead-acid pack and a lighter lithium-ion pack.
angle: Honest total-cost-over-life comparison: lead-acid's lower sticker vs lithium's lighter weight, faster charge and longer life. Use the data layer's guidance (above ~60 km/day, choose lithium) as the deciding line.

title: A low-speed electric scooter for seniors in the Tricity: no licence, ride today
imagePrompt: A senior citizen seated comfortably on a low seated step-through electric scooter (Indian e-moped — seat, flat floorboard, small wheels, low seat height) on a quiet Chandigarh sector lane.
angle: Why the no-licence, low-seat, gearless low-speed class suits older riders for short local trips — framed on ease and the ready-to-ride exemption, not on selling a particular scooter.

title: Do you need insurance for a no-RTO electric scooter in Chandigarh, Mohali or Panchkula?
imagePrompt: A seated step-through electric scooter (Indian e-moped — seat, flat floorboard, small wheels) parked on a quiet Chandigarh street, clean daylight.
angle: Walk the genuinely grey area honestly: insurance is not legally mandated for an exempt low-speed scooter, interpretations differ, and enforcement varies across the UT, Punjab and Haryana — so the answer is 'confirm with your local RTO', not a flat yes/no.

title: Keeping a low-speed electric scooter healthy through a Tricity monsoon and summer
imagePrompt: A seated step-through electric scooter (Indian e-moped — seat, flat floorboard, small wheels) parked under shelter during light Chandigarh monsoon rain, wet sector road.
angle: Seasonal ownership advice specific to the Tricity climate — wet-season riding and storage, summer heat and battery care — practical local guidance a generic maintenance answer wouldn't localise.

title: पहला इलेक्ट्रिक स्कूटर कैसे चुनें — आसान गाइड (Tricity)
imagePrompt: A first-time rider standing beside a parked seated step-through electric scooter (Indian e-moped — seat, flat floorboard, small wheels) on a calm Chandigarh sector street, daytime.
angle: बोलचाल की हिंदी में: रोज़ की दूरी के हिसाब से 'bina license wala scooter' चुनना — battery (lead-acid बनाम lithium), range और 'ghar pe charge' की बात; किसी एक मॉडल की बिक्री नहीं, पूरी कैटेगरी की सलाह।

factCheckIssues.claim: Low-speed scooter की full charge में करीब **2 units** बिजली लगती है। ₹5/unit के realistic average से: > **एक full charge ≈ ₹10**
factCheckIssues.problem: The data layer specifies 'full_charge_units': '~2' and 'full_charge_cost_inr': '10', which is consistent with the article's claim. However, the article should note that this ~₹10 figure assumes the ~₹5/unit all-in basis (including fixed charges, duty, etc.), not just the energy charge alone. The phrasing is acceptable but could be slightly clearer that this is an all-in average.

factCheckIssues.claim: Chandigarh में domestic electricity का rate tiered है — सबसे कम slab पर करीब ₹2.75/unit, बीच के slab पर करीब ₹4.80/unit, और ऊपर जाने पर ₹5.40/unit तक।
factCheckIssues.problem: The data layer states the tiered rates for Chandigarh JERC tariff, which aligns with the article's claim. However, the article should reinforce more clearly (as it does later) that ₹5/unit is a realistic all-in average that accounts for fixed charges and duty, not just the energy component, to prevent readers from expecting to charge at the lowest slab rate exclusively.

factCheckIssues.claim: Mandatory insurance | नहीं* | हाँ | *CMVR के मुताबिक, low-speed exempt scooters पर insurance legally mandatory नहीं है, हालाँकि कुछ लोग MV Act की अलग interpretation करते हैं। अपने local RTO से confirm करें।
factCheckIssues.problem: The data layer's insurance_note warns that 'some interpretations argue third-party cover is still required under the MV Act, and on-ground enforcement varies' — the article's phrasing is consistent with this nuance. However, the table presents 'नहीं' (no) as a binary claim, which could be misread by some as absolute. The footnote and RTO confirmation directive mitigate this, but the table entry itself lacks the necessary qualifier.

factCheckIssues.claim: ऊपर दी गई prices approximate हैं और lead-acid बनाम lithium variant, और आपके state (Chandigarh/Mohali/Panchkula) के हिसाब से बदल सकती हैं। Showroom जाकर exact ex-showroom price confirm करें।
factCheckIssues.problem: This is good practice and consistent with the models.json 'verify_before_publish' directive, which flags that prices must be verified against live Zelio site and local pricing. The article correctly instructs readers to confirm at showroom, which is prudent given the data is marked as draft and subject to change.

factCheckIssues.claim: Zelio Little Gracy जैसे models इस category में आते हैं — हल्के, कम seat height, नए riders के लिए ठीक | Budget: ₹45,000-55,000 के आसपास
factCheckIssues.problem: The models.json data lists Little Gracy at 'price_from_inr': 45633, which is just above ₹45,000. The article's range of '₹45,000-55,000' is reasonable but should either cite the exact entry price (₹45,633) or note that it varies by variant. This is a minor precision issue, not a factual error.

factCheckIssues.claim: Zelio Gracy i जैसे all-round daily commuter models इस range में हैं | Budget: ₹55,000-70,000 के आसपास
factCheckIssues.problem: The models.json lists Gracy i at 'price_from_inr': 56825, which is above ₹55,000. The upper bound of ₹70,000 is not explicitly justified by the data provided. The article should either cite the exact starting price or note that the range reflects different battery variants (lead-acid vs lithium).

factCheckIssues.claim: Zelio Logix जैसे cargo-friendly models delivery work के लिए बने हैं | Budget: ₹60,000-80,000 के आसपास
factCheckIssues.problem: The models.json lists Logix at 'price_from_inr': 61584, which is slightly above ₹60,000. The upper bound of ₹80,000 is not provided in the data. The article should verify the top-end price of the Logix (especially the highest lithium variant) before publication, as the data notes 'verify exact range of top variant'.
